# SPD-019 — Render should survive Obsidian rewriting a rendered note's frontmatter

## Brief
Obsidian normalises YAML frontmatter in notes Eric opens, and the render then refuses the file as hand-edited (exit 6), which stops the ledger commit until Spud runs `render --discard`. Evidence, 2026-09-12: `ledger/tickets/SPD-015.md` was rendered at 20:00:47 and rewritten at 20:04 with `title: "…"` unquoted and `tags: [ticket, ledger-v1]` expanded to a block list, nothing else changed; no render event between those times and no agent can write under `ledger/` (the edit hook refuses everyone), so the writer was Obsidian with the vault open on the active ticket. The hash check is doing its job; the question is what counts as a hand edit. Options: compare parsed frontmatter plus body instead of the raw bytes, so a pure style rewrite renders silently; or emit frontmatter in the style Obsidian normalises to, so there is nothing to rewrite; or keep the hash and let `render` auto-discard when the only difference is YAML style, naming it in the event. Done when: a rendered note whose frontmatter Obsidian has normalised renders without a conflict, a real hand edit of a value or the body still conflicts, and a test covers both.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer; tier decided when it starts. No Fable on 2026-09-12.
